title: repository.bootstrap registers the product in the manager catalog against paths that actually exist
description:
FILED BY worker-1d53e70c FROM task-80322112a48d44c69c6c55f846f8d43f (child 3, the browser proof), 2026-09-06 16:20Z, under SPIDR parent task-5ef1a0a9010c4bfe872ff9b774068234. task-80322112 dependsOn this row and is BLOCKED on it. The defect is in child 2's file (task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9, DONE and landed) - full finding with probe source and control in comment-710d0b5656154f07abaedd7273aa4508 on that row.

THE DEFECT, MEASURED NOT READ. `repository.bootstrap` CANNOT SUCCEED ON A REAL FILESYSTEM. Every local-only run reaches the last effect and answers BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED / CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED, after the repository has already been created, committed and BOUND. An operator is told the bootstrap failed while holding a perfectly good bound repository - the exact harm child 3 exists to prevent, arriving from a different direction.

WHERE. apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts:174-179 wires registerCatalog with configPath `${dir}/moe.config.json` and storePath `${dir}/.moe-next/store.sqlite`. NOTHING ON THE BOOTSTRAP PATH CREATES EITHER. `git grep -n "moe\.config\.json" apps/daemon/src` outside tests returns exactly two hits: cli/moe-init.ts:34 (names the constant) and :176 (consumes it). The controlled-profile scaffold emits neither (its set is package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml, tsconfig.base.json, vite.config.ts, playwright.config.ts, docker-compose.yml, .gitignore, .env.example, README.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, migrations/, e2e/, packages/api/*, packages/web/*).

project-catalog.ts:127-140 canonicalEntry realpaths configPath and dirname(storePath); both ENOENT (root RESOLVES), so it refuses PROJECT_CATALOG_PATH_UNRESOLVED; project-catalog-registrar.ts:67 THROWS it; repository-bootstrap-service.ts:66-67 catches a throwing port and answers BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED.

PROBE OUTPUT with a discriminating control (real registrar, node v24 type-stripping, probe deleted in the same call; full source in the child-2 comment):
  A_SCAFFOLD_SHAPED_INPUT: THREW ProjectCatalogRefusalError PROJECT_CATALOG_PATH_UNRESOLVED
  CONTROL_PATHS_EXIST: REGISTERED_OK

WHY EVERY EXISTING ARM IS GREEN. repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts:114 takes `Omit<RepositoryBootstrapSeams, "catalog">` and :127 stubs `catalog:` with an in-memory recorder, so the real createNodeProjectCatalogRegistrar and its realpath requirement are never exercised - including by :241 "SUCCEEDS local-only with gh absent: committed, bound, catalogued".

RECOMMENDED SHAPE, for the architect to confirm or overrule. Fix it in the composition at :174-179: create moe.config.json and .moe-next/ before registerCatalog, reusing cli/moe-init.ts which already knows the config format. NOT in the scaffold - moe.config.json and .moe-next are MOE's own project files, not files of the generated product. NOT in canonicalEntry - loosening the realpath contract weakens the catalog for every other caller and would let a typo register.

SCOPE: apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts plus its arms, and whatever cli/moe-init.ts must export to be reused. Small.
definitionOfDone: repository.bootstrap completes a local-only bootstrap against a REAL filesystem and a REAL catalog registrar: outcome BOOTSTRAPPED, refusal null, githubRefusal null, and the product present in the catalog file on disk. Asserted with the `catalog` seam NOT stubbed - a stub is precisely what hid this defect (repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts:114,127).

The failing path keeps its stable code: when the catalog genuinely cannot be written (e.g. an unwritable catalog path), the receipt still answers BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED / CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED and the local repository is still retained. Assert the CODE, not merely that it refused, and name which layer refused.

A mutation drill proves the new arm is not vacuous: remove whatever now creates moe.config.json / .moe-next and confirm the arm reds with PROJECT_CATALOG_PATH_UNRESOLVED reaching BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED. Restore proven by sha256 against an out-of-tree backup in a call separate from the restore (untracked paths are invisible to `git diff`).

The commit count is unchanged: a local-only bootstrap still leaves EXACTLY ONE commit in the new repository. Whatever writes moe.config.json / .moe-next must either land inside the single scaffold commit or be gitignored - `git log --oneline` = 1 line is task-80322112's DoD 2 and must not be broken by this fix.
Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`. An exit-0 leg with no `Test Files N passed` count line ran nothing.
taskRails: THE LOCAL REPOSITORY IS ALREADY REAL WHEN THIS STEP RUNS. Bind has already succeeded. Never turn a catalog failure into a message that reads as total failure, and never delete or roll back the operator's committed repository to make a failure path tidy.

DO NOT LOOSEN `canonicalEntry` (project-catalog.ts:127-140). Its realpath contract protects every catalog caller from registering a path that does not exist; the bug is that bootstrap names paths it never creates, not that the catalog is too strict.
DO NOT STUB THE `catalog` SEAM IN THE ARM THAT PROVES THIS. The existing stub at repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts:127 is the entire reason a command that can never succeed shipped green.
EXACTLY ONE COMMIT must remain in a freshly bootstrapped repository - task-80322112's Playwright journey asserts the LINE COUNT of `git log --oneline`, not merely that a commit exists.

implementationPlan.description:
**REPRODUCE THE FAILURE AGAINST A REAL REGISTRAR. NO EDITS.** worker-1d53e70c's probe is in `comment-710d0b56` on task-facff1d1 with full source — read it first rather than re-deriving.

(a) **CONFIRM THE DEFECT AT YOUR HEAD.** Drive a local-only `repository.bootstrap` with the `catalog` seam NOT stubbed — the real `createNodeProjectCatalogRegistrar`. Expect `BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED` / `CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED` after the repository is created, committed and bound. **Quote the receipt.** If it now succeeds, a peer has fixed it and this row should be closed rather than re-fixed — report that.

(b) **CONFIRM THE TWO PATHS ARE UNPRODUCED**: `git grep -n "moe\.config\.json" apps/daemon/src` excluding tests should return exactly two hits (`cli/moe-init.ts:34` declares, `repository-bootstrap-command.ts:176` consumes) and the controlled-profile root set should contain neither `moe.config.json` nor `.moe-next`.

(c) **RECORD THE EFFECT ORDER** in `repository-bootstrap-service.ts`: prepare -> write -> **git.commit (`add -A`)** -> github -> bind -> registerCatalog. Step 2's timing decision depends on it, and `createBootstrapGitPort`'s `add -A` is what makes "before the commit" dangerous.

(d) **RECORD THE GENERATED `.gitignore` LINES** and the `GOLDEN_MANIFEST` row for `.gitignore` plus `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT`. Step 2 moves exactly that one sha and nothing else; these are the before-values.

(e) **READ `cli/moe-init.ts`'s REUSE SURFACE**: `MOE_CONFIG_FILENAME` (`:34`), `MOE_CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`:35`), `planInit` (`:138`, computes `configPath` at `:155`), `parseMoeConfig` (`:191`). **There is no exported writer** — confirm that, and note the config SHAPE `parseMoeConfig` accepts, because the file you write must parse back through it.

(f) **CONFIRM THE INTERACTION THAT DECIDES GITIGNORE**: `moe-init.ts:144-145` refuses `MOE_INIT_CONFIG_PRESENT` when `moe.config.json` is already present. That is why step 2 gitignores the config rather than committing it — verify it still holds.

(g) **BASELINE THE GATES.** Cite a fleet-shared BEFORE (holder, task, timestamps, sha, count line) rather than queueing for a lease; disclose HEAD drift. `pnpm typecheck` is cheap and unleased — run it fresh.

**THE FIX.** `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts` (the composition at `:170-179`) and ONE line in `apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/controlled-profile-root-templates.ts`.

**CREATE `moe.config.json` AND `.moe-next/` BEFORE `registerCatalog` RUNS, AND AFTER `git.commit`.** The timing is the decision:
- **After the commit**, because `createBootstrapGitPort` runs `add -A` — creating them earlier would commit **`.moe-next/store.sqlite`, a SQLite database, into the operator's brand-new repository** (risk D).
- **Before `registerCatalog`**, because `canonicalEntry` realpaths `configPath` and `dirname(storePath)` and refuses `PROJECT_CATALOG_PATH_UNRESOLVED` if either is absent.

**ADD `.moe-next/` AND `moe.config.json` TO THE GENERATED `.gitignore`** (currently `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.env`, `*.log`, `playwright-report/`, `test-results/`). This is the one scaffold edit the row makes, and it is about what the product repo TRACKS rather than what the product IS — so it does not breach rail 3's "not in the scaffold".

**WHY THE CONFIG IS GITIGNORED RATHER THAN COMMITTED, and this is the call to overrule if the product disagrees:** `moe-init.ts:144-145` refuses `MOE_INIT_CONFIG_PRESENT` when `moe.config.json` is already in the target. A committed config would make `moe init` REFUSE on a fresh clone of that product. Write that reasoning into the code comment so the next reader can re-open it deliberately rather than by accident.

**REUSE `cli/moe-init.ts`'s CONSTANTS, NOT A COPY.** Import `MOE_CONFIG_FILENAME` and `MOE_CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION`; do not retype either literal. The file you write MUST parse back through `parseMoeConfig` — assert that in step 3 rather than trusting the shape.

**DO NOT TOUCH `canonicalEntry`** (rail 2) and **DO NOT ADD THESE TO THE CONTROLLED PROFILE'S FILE SET** (rail 3). The scaffold emits the product; these are Moe's own files.

**THE FAILING PATH IS UNCHANGED** (rail 1, DoD 2): when the catalog genuinely cannot be written the receipt still answers `BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED` / `CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED`, and the local repository is RETAINED. This row makes the success path reachable; it does not soften the failure path, and it never deletes the operator's repository to tidy one.

**THE ARMS — WITH THE `catalog` SEAM NOT STUBBED.** `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts`.

**(A) DoD 1 — A LOCAL-ONLY BOOTSTRAP SUCCEEDS END TO END** against a REAL filesystem and the REAL `createNodeProjectCatalogRegistrar`: `outcome: "BOOTSTRAPPED"`, `refusal: null`, `githubRefusal: null`, **and the product present in the catalog file on disk**. Read the catalog back from disk rather than trusting the registrar's return.

**THE SEAM MUST NOT BE STUBBED HERE** (rail 3, risk A). `:114` takes `Omit<RepositoryBootstrapSeams, "catalog">` and `:127` stubs it — that stub is why a command that can never succeed shipped green. This arm composes the real registrar. **`:241` ("SUCCEEDS local-only with gh absent: committed, bound, catalogued") currently asserts a success that cannot happen** — reconcile it: either point it at the real registrar too, or make its stubbed scope explicit in its name so it stops reading as proof of the thing it does not prove.

**(B) DoD 4 — EXACTLY ONE COMMIT.** `git log --oneline` in the new repository returns **exactly one line**. Assert the LINE COUNT, not that a commit exists — task-80322112's journey asserts the count and this fix must not break it.

**(C) THE STORE IS NOT COMMITTED.** `git ls-files` in the new repository contains **no `.moe-next/` path and no `moe.config.json`**, and `git status --porcelain` is CLEAN (both are gitignored). This is the arm that catches the timing mistake: create them before `add -A` and a database rides into the operator's first commit.

**(D) THE CONFIG PARSES BACK.** The written `moe.config.json` round-trips through `parseMoeConfig` (`moe-init.ts:191`) without refusal. A file that satisfies the catalog's realpath but is not a valid Moe config would pass (A) and be useless.

**(E) DoD 2 — THE FAILING PATH KEEPS ITS CODE.** With a genuinely unwritable catalog path, the receipt still answers `BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED` / `CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED`, naming the layer that refused, **and the local repository is still on disk with its commit intact**. Assert the code and the retention, not merely that it refused.

**THE GOLDEN, DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW.**

**(a) THE GOLDEN MOVES BY EXACTLY ONE ROW.** Run `controlled-profile-generator.test.ts`. `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT` stays **22**; only `.gitignore`'s sha in `GOLDEN_MANIFEST` moves, and it moves because this change requires it. Re-pin that ONE row and quote the before/after sha. **Any other file's sha moving means something leaked into the scaffold — stop and investigate rather than re-pinning** (risk G).

**(b) DRILLS.** `git status --porcelain` every path first and RECORD it. Back EVERY mutated path up **out of tree**; restore FROM THE BACKUP, never `git checkout --`; prove by **SHA256 in a call SEPARATE from the restore**. DoD 3 is explicit that the new arm's paths are untracked and therefore invisible to `git diff` — sha256 is the only proof that works there.

THREE MUTATIONS, each alone, the named arm confirmed RED, then restored:
1. **Remove whatever now creates `moe.config.json` / `.moe-next`** -> arm (A) reds with `PROJECT_CATALOG_PATH_UNRESOLVED` reaching `BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED`. **DoD 3's named drill** — it reproduces the shipped defect exactly and proves the new arm is not vacuous.
2. **Move the creation to BEFORE `git.commit`** -> arm (C) reds: the store is committed. This proves the timing decision is guarded rather than incidental.
3. **Remove `.moe-next/` from the generated `.gitignore`** -> arm (C) reds on the dirty-tree half. Proves the scaffold line is load-bearing.

**(c) GATES.** `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`, standalone and foreground. **RECORDED** verification is the scoped owned command at exit 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line and every filter or env flag INSIDE the recorded string; the repo-wide legs are **DISCLOSED** with exit codes, failing-file sets and the `(AFTER - BEFORE) INTERSECT owned = empty` computation. New-since-BEFORE is not automatically foreign — compute the intersection. Root `pnpm test` covers no `apps/**` file.

**(d) ADVERSARIAL PASS** — answer each in writing:
- **Is anything Moe writes now inside the operator's first commit?** `git ls-files` the new repo and read the list.
- **Does a fresh clone of the product still work with `moe init`?** State what `moe-init.ts:144-145` does given your gitignore choice.
- **Does the failure path still retain the repository?** Force it and confirm the commit survives.
- **Did the catalog entry register against paths that exist**, or did it pass because the test reused an existing directory? Assert on a directory the test created this run.
- **Is `canonicalEntry` untouched?** `git diff` `project-catalog.ts` must be empty.

**(e)** DECLARE EVERY PATH in `complete_step.modifiedFiles`; re-check `git status --porcelain` for anything unreported, mutate-and-restore paths included, which must show CLEAN.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
**worker-1d53e70c's DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED AND THEIR RECOMMENDED SHAPE IS ADOPTED, with one addition they did not cover that would otherwise commit a database into the operator's repository.**

I re-measured the three load-bearing facts rather than reading them:
- `git grep -n "moe\.config\.json" apps/daemon/src` (tests excluded) = **exactly two hits**: `cli/moe-init.ts:34` declares the constant, `repository-bootstrap-command.ts:176` consumes it. **Nothing produces it.**
- The controlled-profile root set is `.env.example`, `.gitignore`, `docker-compose.yml`, `package.json`, `playwright.config.ts`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `tsconfig.base.json` (+ README, CI). **No `moe.config.json`, no `.moe-next`.**
- So `canonicalEntry`'s realpath refuses, the registrar throws, and the service answers `BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED`. Every local-only bootstrap.

**THEIR THREE PLACEMENT CALLS ARE RIGHT AND I AM KEEPING ALL THREE.** Fix in the composition at `:174-179`; NOT in the scaffold (these are Moe's files, not the generated product's); NOT in `canonicalEntry` (loosening realpath would let a typo register for every caller).

**THE FORK THEY DID NOT COVER: WHEN, relative to the single commit — and it decides whether a SQLite store lands in the operator's repository.** `bootstrapRepository` runs prepare -> write -> **git.commit (`add -A`)** -> github -> bind -> registerCatalog. The recommendation says "before registerCatalog", which is AFTER the commit. Both timings pass DoD 4's literal `git log --oneline` = 1 check, but they differ sharply:
- **BEFORE the commit:** `add -A` sweeps in `.moe-next/store.sqlite`. **The generated `.gitignore` does NOT list `.moe-next/`** — it is exactly `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.env`, `*.log`, `playwright-report/`, `test-results/`. So a database file would be committed into a brand-new product repository.
- **AFTER the commit:** both paths are left UNTRACKED, so the operator's fresh repository is dirty from birth.

**DECIDED: create both AFTER the commit AND add `.moe-next/` to the generated `.gitignore`.** Clean tree, no database committed, and DoD 4's "or be gitignored" branch is satisfied explicitly rather than by accident.

**AND `moe.config.json` IS GITIGNORED TOO — on a measured interaction, not a preference.** `moe-init.ts:144-145` refuses `MOE_INIT_CONFIG_PRESENT` when the file is already in the target directory. If bootstrap committed it, `moe init` on a fresh clone of that product would REFUSE. That is a real downstream break, so the config is a per-checkout file and belongs in `.gitignore` beside the store. **If the product intends the config to be committed, this is the call to overrule** — the reasoning is stated so it can be.

**COST, stated up front: this moves ONE golden pin** — `.gitignore`'s sha in `GOLDEN_MANIFEST`. That is a pin move the change genuinely requires, and the row owns it. No other file's sha may move.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04) BY ME.

1. **THE COMPOSITION**, `repository-bootstrap-command.ts:170-179`:
```ts
registerCatalog: async (repository) => {
  await options.catalog({
    configPath: `${repository.dir}/moe.config.json`, projectId: repository.projectId,
    root: repository.dir, storePath: `${repository.dir}/.moe-next/store.sqlite`,
    title: repository.productName,
  });
},
```

2. **THE EFFECT ORDER** in `bootstrapRepository` (repository-bootstrap-service.ts): `tree.prepare` -> `generateControlledProfile` -> `tree.write` -> **`git.commit`** -> `githubHalf` -> `bindRepository` -> `registerCatalog`. `createBootstrapGitPort` runs `init`, **`add -A`**, `commit`, `rev-parse` — so anything on disk before that commit is swept into it.

3. **THE GENERATED `.gitignore`, in full**: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.env`, `*.log`, `playwright-report/`, `test-results/`. **No `.moe-next/`, no `moe.config.json`.**

4. **`moe-init.ts` IS A PLANNER AND A READER, NOT A WRITER.** `planInit(inputs)` at `:138` resolves the plan and computes `configPath` at `:155`; `parseMoeConfig(raw)` at `:191` reads one back; `MOE_CONFIG_FILENAME` `:34` and `MOE_CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION` `:35` are the constants. **There is no exported config writer to call** — reuse means the CONSTANTS and the SHAPE `parseMoeConfig` accepts, with the write itself new. Do not duplicate the schema version literal.

5. **THE INTERACTION THAT DECIDES GITIGNORE**: `moe-init.ts:144-145` — `if (probe.entries.includes(MOE_CONFIG_FILENAME)) refusals.push(refusal(MOE_INIT_CONFIG_PRESENT, MOE_CONFIG_FILENAME))`. A committed config makes `moe init` refuse on a fresh clone.

6. **WHY EVERY EXISTING ARM IS GREEN** (worker-1d53e70c's finding, and the reason this shipped): `repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts:114` takes `Omit<RepositoryBootstrapSeams, "catalog">` and `:127` stubs `catalog:` with an in-memory recorder. The real `createNodeProjectCatalogRegistrar` and its realpath requirement are exercised by nothing — **including by `:241` "SUCCEEDS local-only with gh absent: committed, bound, catalogued"**, which asserts a success that cannot happen.

7. **THE GOLDEN**: `controlled-profile-generator.test.ts` pins `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT = 22` and a per-file sha `GOLDEN_MANIFEST`. Editing `.gitignore` moves exactly that one row; the file COUNT stays 22.
planningNotes.risks:
A. **DO NOT STUB THE `catalog` SEAM IN THE ARM THAT PROVES THIS** (rail 3). The stub at `repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts:127` is the entire reason a command that can never succeed shipped green, and `:241` currently asserts a success that does not happen. The new arm composes the REAL `createNodeProjectCatalogRegistrar`.

B. **DO NOT LOOSEN `canonicalEntry`** (rail 2, project-catalog.ts:127-140). Its realpath contract protects every catalog caller from registering a path that does not exist. The bug is that bootstrap names paths it never creates.

C. **DO NOT PUT THESE IN THE SCAFFOLD.** `moe.config.json` and `.moe-next` are MOE's files, not the generated product's. The one scaffold edit this row makes is the `.gitignore` LINE, which is about what the product repo tracks — a different question from what the product IS.

D. **NEVER COMMIT A DATABASE.** If the paths are created before `git.commit`'s `add -A`, `.moe-next/store.sqlite` lands in the operator's first commit. Create AFTER the commit and gitignore both.

E. **EXACTLY ONE COMMIT** (rail 4, and task-80322112's DoD 2 asserts the LINE COUNT of `git log --oneline`). Creating files after the commit leaves the count at one; verify it rather than assuming.

F. **THE FAILING PATH KEEPS ITS CODE** (DoD 2). When the catalog genuinely cannot be written, the receipt still answers `BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED` / `CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED` and the local repository is RETAINED. Never delete or roll back the operator's committed repository to tidy a failure path (rail 1).

G. **ONE GOLDEN PIN MOVES AND ONLY ONE.** `.gitignore`'s sha in `GOLDEN_MANIFEST`; `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT` stays 22. Any other file's sha moving means something leaked into the scaffold — stop and investigate rather than re-pinning.

H. **SHARED-TREE RESTORE RULE**: back every mutated path up out of tree, restore FROM THE BACKUP, prove by SHA256 in a separate call. Never `git checkout --`. The new arm's paths are untracked and invisible to `git diff` (DoD 3 says so explicitly).
